question.leadin: The Lateran Treaty governed the relationship between this country and its much larger neighbor.
question.text: Name this country, whose flag and coat of arms both depict a pair of crossed keys. Its head of state is elected through a conclave by the College of Cardinals.
question.answerHtml: Vatican City [or the Vatican City State, or Status Civitatis Vaticanae, or Stato della Città del Vaticano; prompt on the Holy See]
question.clue: A meeting in this city declared that doctrines issued ex cathedra are infallible, and was prompted by the Syllabus of Errors of Pius IX.

swap.text: This pope, who served during World War II, has been called "Hitler's Pope" for not doing enough to stop the Holocaust.
swap.clue: While on trial, Karl Wolff testified that he had been ordered to kidnap this leader, who gave a "Christmas Broadcast" in support of one group who had "been consigned to death or to a slow decline".

question.leadin: Due to their military-like structure, members of this group are sometimes called "God's Marines."
question.text: Name this Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius Loyola. Members of this group included Francis Xavier, who traveled to Japan as a missionary.
question.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

swap.leadin: This term sometimes refers to the period of antipopes during the Avignon Papacy.
swap.text: Name this term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.
swap.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the investiture controversy.
question.text: The controversy over appointing bishops was sparked by the reforms launched by the seventh pope of this name. The thirteenth pope of this name created the modern calendar.
question.clue: Those two theologians with this name are from Nyssa and Nazianzus, and are considered "Cappadocian fathers" along with Basil the Great.

swap.leadin: This council was preceded by a failed attempt at Pisa.
swap.text: Name this church council that ended the Western Schism and burned Jan Hus burned at the stake for promoting Utraquism. Much to the ire of Martin V and other popes, it declared that future councils should meet every 10 years.
swap.clue: Other decisions included the canonization of St. Bridget of Sweden and a voting of special privilege to Emperor Sigismund, who had called this meeting.

question.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
question.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
question.clue: This man officially condemned Liberation Theology, and he unofficially supported the Solidarity movement in his home country.

swap.leadin: Catherine of Siena unsuccessfully appealed to one leader in this city to relocate.
swap.text: Name this city, where a rival papacy was established during the Western Schism. Petrarch ["pet-rark"] compared this city's eponymous papacy to the Babylonian Captivity.
swap.clue: This city was called "a sewer where all the muck of the universe collects" by Petrarch, who coined an enduring Biblical nickname for it.

question.leadin: It also dealt with the Clunian reforms of the Church.
question.text: Name this 1095 council that, more notably, called the First Crusade.
question.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

swap.leadin: Moderator note: do not read the alternate answers to the first part. Stefan Zweig characterized a commander of this organization named Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon as a "half-pirate, half-scientist."
swap.text: Name this military order founded by Italian merchants from Amalfi in 11th century Jerusalem to care for sick and poor pilgrims.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [or the Order of Saint John of Jerusalem or Order of the Hospital of Saint John of Jerusalem or Sovereign Military and Hospitaller Order of Saint John of Jerusalem, of Rhodes, and of Malta; accept Order of Malta]
swap.clue: This group, founded by the Blessed Gerard, controlled the fortresses of Margat (mar-GAH) and Krak des Chevaliers ("crack" deh sheh-val-YAY) before it was forced from the Holy Land.

question.text: Luther was excommunicated by the 10th pope of this name. Another pope with this name convinced Genseric I of the Vandals to not burn the ancient city of Rome in the 5th century.
question.clue: The first Pope with this name was able to convince Attila the Hun not to sack Rome, although his methods may have involved bribery.

swap.leadin: Hundreds of members of this group were arrested on October 13, 1307, which may have contributed to the idea that Friday the 13th is unlucky.
swap.text: Name this group whose leader Jacques de Molay was burned at the stake on the orders of Philip IV of France and Pope Clement V, who regarded this group as a bunch of heretics; both Clement and Philip died less than a year later.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Templar [or Templars; or Order of Solomon's Temple; or Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon]
swap.clue: At the Battle of Montgisard, they helped defeat Saladin's army, and they were founded after the First Crusade by Hugues de Payens and Godfrey de Saint-Omer to protect pilgrims traveling to the Holy Land.

question.text: The fifth pope to take this name suppressed the Templars at the Council of Vienne and moved the papacy to Avignon, thus beginning the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

swap.text: One of these splits in the Christian church arose when Gregory XI moved the papacy back to Rome. The split between the Orthodox and Catholic church in 1054 is known as the "Great" one of these.
swap.clue: This breaks and splits in the Christian church. The "Great" one resulted in the formation of the Catholic Church, while the "Western" one saw three popes ruling simultaneously.

question.leadin: Identify the following ecumenical councils from their theological statements.
question.text: This unrecognized council of 1409 failed to end the Western Schism, and its decision was superseded by the later Council of Constance.
question.clue: It was presided over by the Bishop of Palestrina, and came to a climax with a stirring denunciation delivered by Simon de Cramaud, the Patriarch of Alexandria, after which Baldassare Cossa successfully intrigued on behalf of Peter Philarghi.

swap.leadin: This pope probably died of injuries associated with a painful fall from his mule at Narni.
swap.text: This 14th century Pope once complained that he couldn't hear enough screaming when some rebellious cardinals were being tortured. He was opposed by Antipope Clement VII during the Western Schism.

question.text: Saint Catherine of Siena persuaded this pope to move the papacy back to Rome. This pope also hired John Hawkwood to fight on his behalf in the War of the Eight Saints.
question.answerHtml: Pope <u>Gregory XI</u> [or Pierre-Roger de <u>Beaufort</u>; prompt on “<u>Gregory</u>”]

swap.leadin: This successor of Pius IX had the third-longest pontificate after John Paul II and Pius IX, and was known as the "Rosary Pope" because of his promotion of that prayer.
swap.text: Name this pope who addressed Industrial Revolution-era socio-economic issues and rejected both socialism and unrestrained capitalism in the encyclical Rerum Novarum.
swap.answerHtml: Leo XIII [or Vincenzo Gioacchino Raffaele Luigi Pecci; prompt on “Leo”]
swap.clue: Known as the "Rosary Pope" for his championing of the rosary prayer, this man was the first pope to establish Mary as Mediatrix.

question.leadin: This guy was born Pietro del Murrone, FTPE.
question.text: Elected after the two year power vacuum following the death of Nicholas IV, this since-canonized pope lent his name to a subset of Benedictine ascetics. He grew weary of being manipulated for the political ends of Charles II of Naples and ultimately abdicated the papacy.
question.clue: This pope, the last of his name, was the last elected outside of a conclave. It was he who decreed the right of the pope to abdicate and then did so allowing the ascension of Boniface VIII.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a storied fighting force, FTPE.
swap.text: Kaspar von Silenen headed the first company of soldiers from this troop that was summoned by Julius II to protect the Vatican, a duty it still holds today.
swap.clue: Jakob Fugger financed the formation of this entity in 1506 by the request of Julius II.
